item.title: US Military Hits Targets Near Iran’s Kharg Island
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Michael Allen, former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, says the US is taking its economic pressure campaign against Iran “right to the jugular,” describing Kharg Island as the “Achilles’ heel of the Iranian oil system.” Greta Peisch, former general counsel for the Office of the United States Trade Representative, says the US and Canada are showing restraint in their trade dispute, with critical and sensitive sectors remaining untouched despite room for further escalation. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), senior member of House Appropriations Committee and former Chair of the DNC, says she has serious differences with Abdul El-Sayed, but argues Mike Rogers would be a “rubber stamp” for President Donald Trump. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 2026 Midterms: Swing-State GOP Senate Candidates to Speak at Convention
item.description: Several Republican candidates in hotly contested US Senate races will take center stage at the Dallas GOP convention this week, a decision that will tie them closer to President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: Rep. Wasserman Schultz: Centrists are Path to Retaking the House
item.description: Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), senior member of House Appropriations Committee and former Chair of the DNC, says she has serious differences with Abdul El-Sayed, but argues Mike Rogers would be a “rubber stamp” for President Donald Trump. Rep. Wasserman Schultz says centrists are the path for Democrats to retake the House, while candidates further to the left are winning in solidly blue areas. She also says Democrats are advancing proposals aimed at lowering housing costs. She speaks with Tyler Kendall on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Peisch: Restraint Shown by US and Canada in Trade Disputes
item.description: Greta Peisch, former general counsel for the Office of the United States Trade Representative, says the US and Canada are showing restraint in their trade dispute, with critical and sensitive sectors remaining untouched despite room for further escalation. Peisch says Canada deepening ties with China in strategic and sensitive sectors could cause concern in the US and says Canadian efforts to diversify trade are a difficult, long-term proposition. She speaks with Tyler Kendall on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Allen Doesn't See 'Imminent Return To Negotiations' With Iran
item.description: Michael Allen, former special assistant to President George W. Bush in the National Security sector, says the US is taking its economic pressure campaign against Iran “right to the jugular,” describing Kharg Island as the “Achilles’ heel of the Iranian oil system.” Allen says he doesn't see an “imminent return to negotiations” and argues the US needs a more comprehensive strategy for dealing with China, Russia, Iran and North Korea. He speaks with Tyler Kendall on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Says Trump May Speed Deficit Cut Plans if Democrats Win
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Trump administration would try to plan to lower the federal budget deficit through Congress by the end of this year if Democrats are able to flip either chambers in the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy

item.title: Newsom’s Data-Center Stance Could Define His 2028
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom, who has close ties to Silicon Valley, is facing some tough calls about regulating AI data centers. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Erika D. Smith says his decision could finally cast him as a populist — or further entrench his appearance as a member of so-called elite. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada Tries to Find Alternative Trading Allies
item.description: Canada is trying to secure a new trading alliance with the European Union as its relationship with the US deteriorates. Mark Carney just imposed retaliatory tariffs of 15% to 50% on hundreds of American goods on Tuesday. Bloomberg's Thomas Seal has more from Vancouver. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran, Oil, Canada & U.S. Trade Tensions
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are RBC Capital Markets Head of Derivatives Strategy Amy Wu Silverman, Canada Chamber of Commerce Principal Economist Andrew DiCapua, Guggenheim Senior Analyst, Retail & E-Commerce Simeon Siegel, Marquee Brands CEO Heath Golden, Westwood Holdings Group CEO Brian Casey, AllianceBernstein Head of Equities Nelson Yu, BIVA CEO Maria Ariza, Panama Canal Administrator Ilya Espino de Marotta, Qualcomm CFO Akash Palkhiwala, Cisco President & Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel, & Kroll CEO Jacob Silverman. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple's $2000+ iPhone, Oil Gain Stokes Inflation Fear | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 9/8/2026
item.description: Around 2020, Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook returned from a trip to Asia unusually energized about a new product category: foldable phones. The project will reach its defining moment on Wednesday, when Apple is poised to unveil its first foldable phone. The introduction will also serve as a debut of sorts for CEO John Ternus, who took the job on Sept. 1. The timing of the leadership transition was meant to help herald a new era for Apple products and allow Ternus to be the one to unveil the foldable device. Bloomberg Managing Editor for Consumer Tech, Mark Gurman reports. Plus, Mia Gindis, Bloomberg News Oil Markets Reporter and Mike McKee, Bloomberg TV and Radio International Economics & Policy Correspondent discuss Brent Oil nearing $100 a barrel as conflict with Iran continues. Finally, Bloomberg Opinions Columnist Marc Champion discusses the latest in the lack of negotiations to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Hits Targets Near Iran's Kharg Island, Fox News Says
item.description: The US launches attacks on targets near Iran's Kharg Island and the port city of Jask according to Fox News. Iranian oil tankers were hit according to the report. This as brent oil prices hover around $100 a barrel. Bloomberg's Kate Sullivan reports from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Colombia Leader Seeks to Be Washington’s Top Ally in the Americas
item.description: President Abelardo de la Espriella said Colombia wants to be the top US ally in the Americas as his government seeks Washington’s support in its fight against organized crime.
item.dc:creator: Eric Martin and Andreina Itriago

item.title: Court Fight Over GOP’s Voting Map in Missouri to Continue
item.description: A federal judge revived a legal fight over the use of a congressional map in Missouri that would favor GOP candidates in the November election, shortly after the US Supreme Court rebuffed efforts by state Republicans to halt plans for an alternative map pushed by Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: El-Sayed Fights Trump Villain Tag | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 9/8/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses the latest from the White House. On today's show, Atlantic Council Senior Fellow Melinda Haring, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Echo Canyon Consulting Founder Jon Seaton and Michigan Democratic Senate Candidate Abdul El-Sayed. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Senate Race Shakes Up the Battle for Senate Control
item.description: A strong Democratic candidate and an imperfect GOP nominee are triggering action from national Republicans.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Trump Plans to Ban Imports of Some Canadian Dairy, Alcohol
item.description: The US escalated its trade war with Canada, moving to block imports of some alcoholic beverages, dairy products and motorcycles, as well as seeking to bar Canadian companies from selling to US government contractors.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: Witkoff Reports $107 Million From Entity That Held Crypto Stake
item.description: President Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff earned $107 million in 2025 from the holding company that owned his share of a crypto venture he and his boss helped co-found, according to a recent financial disclosure report.
item.dc:creator: Bill Allison

item.title: Iran Seizes Underwater Drone That US Forces Say Malfunctioned
item.description: Iran’s military claimed that it captured a state-of-the-art underwater drone from US forces amid ongoing tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, but the US dismissed the sea drone as “defective and malfunctioning,” and said it didn’t have any classified equipment on board.
item.dc:creator: Tony Capaccio

item.title: US Says It Destroyed Iranian Tankers After US Navy Ship Targeted
item.description: US forces destroyed five Iranian tankers carrying crude oil on Tuesday in response to two attempts to hit a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles in as many days, Central Command said.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan and Tony Capaccio

item.title: US Pursues Deportees Abroad for Hundreds of Millions in Unpaid Fines
item.description: The Trump administration is hiring private contractors to track down deported migrants who it claims owe the US government hundreds of millions of dollars in unpaid penalties, a move that will test how far its immigration crackdown can reach across borders.
item.dc:creator: Alicia A. Caldwell and Maya Averbuch
